unresolved_findings.claim: MUST-FIX The new post-claim snapshot block (src/engine/campaign-intake.js, `if (pendingQcPanelSnapshot)`) returns `qc_panel_snapshot_drift`, `qc_panel_snapshot_missing_after_claim`, and the write/read `qc_panel_snapshot_identity_invalid` rejections with a bare `return { status: 'blocked', ..., pre_spend_no_effect_receipt: null }` while a successful `missionClaim` is already held; `releaseAfterRejection` (the base release/no-effect-receipt path used by every other post-claim rejection) is declared below the block and never invoked, so the Mission claim leaks and the "parked, resumable" guarantee in spec §2/§3 is violated on the next resume. Test (b)/(d) never count `releaseMission`, so the suite cannot see it. Smallest fix: perform the stored-vs-recomputed digest check in the pre-claim block (where `existing` is already read and identity-checked) so drift rejects before the claim exactly like identity does, and hoist `releaseAfterRejection` above the post-claim block so the missing-after-claim and write-failure rejections route through it (and add a `releaseMission` count assertion in the new test).

MUST-FIX Engine `snapshotStation` flip check fires when `(roster.qc_panel_seats_complete === true) !== (snapshotStation === 'panel')`; every managed roster has `qc_panel_seats_complete === true` (base `validateReviewRoster` requires it), so any single-station campaign whose 2-C snapshot carries `review_station: 'single'` (in_rail_review not 'panel') now journals a `qc_panel_snapshot_live_flip { sealed_station:'single', live_seats_complete:true }` row on every run, breaking spec §5 byte-identity for single-station campaigns. Smallest fix: resolve the live station with the same rule as `resolveReviewStation` (seats complete AND in_rail_review === 'panel') and journal only when live station !== sealed station; add a single-station control case to the new test asserting no flip row.

CUT/FOLLOW-UP `allowIncompleteQcSeats` is granted on mere existence of `qc_panel_snapshot.json` next to the contract (no identity check) and the early `return roster` skips all remaining seat/terminal-panel validation; only affects rosters that base already rejected, so not blocking, but tie the bypass to a verified snapshot in a later cut.

CUT/FOLLOW-UP blind-dispatch.md now says "identity or digest mismatch parks with `qc_panel_snapshot_drift`", but identity mismatch still rejects pre-claim with `qc_panel_snapshot_identity_invalid` (required to keep `panel-snap-id` byte-identical); reword the doc to name both codes.

CUT/FOLLOW-UP `campaignJournalHasEvents` treats any journal row for the campaign as "post-claim"; a campaign whose earlier generations ran without a snapshot and later presents a complete panel roster is parked forever with `qc_panel_snapshot_missing_after_claim` instead of sealing; acceptable under plan §6 wording, note in backlog.

CUT/FOLLOW-UP Case (e) "projection bytes" projects an empty row list (asserts nothing about base bytes) and case (c) accepts `stationRow || reviewModels.length >= 3`; tighten in a follow-up, no product impact.

CUT/FOLLOW-UP BACKLOG Context line was trimmed (dropped `FINAL_PANEL_SEAT_OPTIONAL_KEYS`/receipt-schema text) rather than appended, and the edited row's Source cites the blind-review-packet plan, so confirm it is the "blind review redesign (1a-B)" row the spec names.

MUST-FIX — both references/blind-dispatch.md copies (root and platforms/codex/plugin mirror, identical patch) say "identity or digest mismatch parks with `qc_panel_snapshot_drift`", but the shipped campaign-intake.js correctly keeps `qc_panel_snapshot_identity_invalid` for campaign_id/contract_digest mismatch (required so the existing `panel-snap-id` case stays byte-identical per the spec's tests section); impact: the normative reference doc misdocuments the park code operators will see on a foreign/foreign-digest file resume, inviting wrong alerting/automation; smallest remediation: reword that one sentence to "digest mismatch parks with `qc_panel_snapshot_drift`; identity mismatch keeps `qc_panel_snapshot_identity_invalid`" in references/blind-dispatch.md and platforms/codex/plugin/references/blind-dispatch.md (mirrors must stay identical).

CUT/FOLLOW-UP — validateReviewRoster's new allowIncompleteQcSeats early-return skips all remaining roster checks (seat-array/family checks and, if ordered after them in the base function, the requireTerminalPanel enforcement) whenever any digest-valid snapshot file — including a pre-2-C file with no review_station that carries no station signal — exists beside the campaign contract; unreachable in the spec's tested live-flip scenario (sealed 2-C panel + incomplete live roster) and gated on campaignRequested + file existence, so excluded from this cut; follow-up hardening: gate the early return on the sealed snapshot actually carrying review_station.

CUT/FOLLOW-UP — new test case (e)'s no-snapshot control asserts `typeof projection === 'string'`, which is vacuous against the spec's "assert the projection bytes"; the meaningful assertions (zero qc_panel_snapshot steps, no result.qc_panel_snapshot) plus the unchanged existing suites pin no-snapshot byte-identity, so it does not block this cut; follow-up: hash-compare the projection against a base-captured fixture.

CUT/FOLLOW-UP — the BACKLOG "blind review redesign" Context line was rewritten ("`FINAL_PANEL_SEAT_OPTIONAL_KEYS` (mixed presence rejected); receipt schema + mirror" → "mixed-presence keys") rather than purely appended; the base line is ~243 B so a pure append cannot satisfy the spec's own ≤240 B limit enforced by check-backlog-entries.js, and the new line is ~203 B with "2-D D2 shipped v2.36.77" appended — accepted as the minimal resolution of that spec conflict, no change requested this cut.

findings_snapshot.claim: MUST-FIX The new post-claim snapshot block (src/engine/campaign-intake.js, `if (pendingQcPanelSnapshot)`) returns `qc_panel_snapshot_drift`, `qc_panel_snapshot_missing_after_claim`, and the write/read `qc_panel_snapshot_identity_invalid` rejections with a bare `return { status: 'blocked', ..., pre_spend_no_effect_receipt: null }` while a successful `missionClaim` is already held; `releaseAfterRejection` (the base release/no-effect-receipt path used by every other post-claim rejection) is declared below the block and never invoked, so the Mission claim leaks and the "parked, resumable" guarantee in spec §2/§3 is violated on the next resume. Test (b)/(d) never count `releaseMission`, so the suite cannot see it. Smallest fix: perform the stored-vs-recomputed digest check in the pre-claim block (where `existing` is already read and identity-checked) so drift rejects before the claim exactly like identity does, and hoist `releaseAfterRejection` above the post-claim block so the missing-after-claim and write-failure rejections route through it (and add a `releaseMission` count assertion in the new test).

MUST-FIX Engine `snapshotStation` flip check fires when `(roster.qc_panel_seats_complete === true) !== (snapshotStation === 'panel')`; every managed roster has `qc_panel_seats_complete === true` (base `validateReviewRoster` requires it), so any single-station campaign whose 2-C snapshot carries `review_station: 'single'` (in_rail_review not 'panel') now journals a `qc_panel_snapshot_live_flip { sealed_station:'single', live_seats_complete:true }` row on every run, breaking spec §5 byte-identity for single-station campaigns. Smallest fix: resolve the live station with the same rule as `resolveReviewStation` (seats complete AND in_rail_review === 'panel') and journal only when live station !== sealed station; add a single-station control case to the new test asserting no flip row.

CUT/FOLLOW-UP `allowIncompleteQcSeats` is granted on mere existence of `qc_panel_snapshot.json` next to the contract (no identity check) and the early `return roster` skips all remaining seat/terminal-panel validation; only affects rosters that base already rejected, so not blocking, but tie the bypass to a verified snapshot in a later cut.

CUT/FOLLOW-UP blind-dispatch.md now says "identity or digest mismatch parks with `qc_panel_snapshot_drift`", but identity mismatch still rejects pre-claim with `qc_panel_snapshot_identity_invalid` (required to keep `panel-snap-id` byte-identical); reword the doc to name both codes.

CUT/FOLLOW-UP `campaignJournalHasEvents` treats any journal row for the campaign as "post-claim"; a campaign whose earlier generations ran without a snapshot and later presents a complete panel roster is parked forever with `qc_panel_snapshot_missing_after_claim` instead of sealing; acceptable under plan §6 wording, note in backlog.

CUT/FOLLOW-UP Case (e) "projection bytes" projects an empty row list (asserts nothing about base bytes) and case (c) accepts `stationRow || reviewModels.length >= 3`; tighten in a follow-up, no product impact.

CUT/FOLLOW-UP BACKLOG Context line was trimmed (dropped `FINAL_PANEL_SEAT_OPTIONAL_KEYS`/receipt-schema text) rather than appended, and the edited row's Source cites the blind-review-packet plan, so confirm it is the "blind review redesign (1a-B)" row the spec names.

MUST-FIX — both references/blind-dispatch.md copies (root and platforms/codex/plugin mirror, identical patch) say "identity or digest mismatch parks with `qc_panel_snapshot_drift`", but the shipped campaign-intake.js correctly keeps `qc_panel_snapshot_identity_invalid` for campaign_id/contract_digest mismatch (required so the existing `panel-snap-id` case stays byte-identical per the spec's tests section); impact: the normative reference doc misdocuments the park code operators will see on a foreign/foreign-digest file resume, inviting wrong alerting/automation; smallest remediation: reword that one sentence to "digest mismatch parks with `qc_panel_snapshot_drift`; identity mismatch keeps `qc_panel_snapshot_identity_invalid`" in references/blind-dispatch.md and platforms/codex/plugin/references/blind-dispatch.md (mirrors must stay identical).

CUT/FOLLOW-UP — validateReviewRoster's new allowIncompleteQcSeats early-return skips all remaining roster checks (seat-array/family checks and, if ordered after them in the base function, the requireTerminalPanel enforcement) whenever any digest-valid snapshot file — including a pre-2-C file with no review_station that carries no station signal — exists beside the campaign contract; unreachable in the spec's tested live-flip scenario (sealed 2-C panel + incomplete live roster) and gated on campaignRequested + file existence, so excluded from this cut; follow-up hardening: gate the early return on the sealed snapshot actually carrying review_station.

CUT/FOLLOW-UP — new test case (e)'s no-snapshot control asserts `typeof projection === 'string'`, which is vacuous against the spec's "assert the projection bytes"; the meaningful assertions (zero qc_panel_snapshot steps, no result.qc_panel_snapshot) plus the unchanged existing suites pin no-snapshot byte-identity, so it does not block this cut; follow-up: hash-compare the projection against a base-captured fixture.

CUT/FOLLOW-UP — the BACKLOG "blind review redesign" Context line was rewritten ("`FINAL_PANEL_SEAT_OPTIONAL_KEYS` (mixed presence rejected); receipt schema + mirror" → "mixed-presence keys") rather than purely appended; the base line is ~243 B so a pure append cannot satisfy the spec's own ≤240 B limit enforced by check-backlog-entries.js, and the new line is ~203 B with "2-D D2 shipped v2.36.77" appended — accepted as the minimal resolution of that spec conflict, no change requested this cut.
